narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

cashier.instruct: Cheerful, slightly bored supermarket cashier, bright and friendly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You walked into the supermarket for one carton of milk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Twenty minutes later, your cart is full and you can't remember why.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You feel calm. The music is soft. Nobody is rushing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You even grabbed a bottle of French wine. You don't drink wine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then a door swings open in the back. The manager is turning a dial marked tempo.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That soft music wasn't for you. It was for your feet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In nineteen eighty-two, a researcher switched a supermarket between slow and fast songs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With slow music, shoppers walked slower down every aisle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And on slow days, sales were thirty-eight percent higher than on fast days.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fast songs did the opposite and hurried people along.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Music can even pick what you buy.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A wine shop played French accordion music one day, German oompah the next.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On French days, seventy-seven percent of the wine sold was French.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On German days, seventy-three percent was German.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Out of forty-four shoppers asked, just one mentioned the music.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the store isn't just playing songs. It's setting your speed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You finally reach the checkout with forty things and no milk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Back in aisle nine, the music gets even slower.
